title: Musée Marmottan Monet: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works on the balance between a recognisable subject and the marks, light and reflections that unsettle it.
introduction:
The harbour in *Impression, Sunrise* is identifiable despite its blurred distance. An orange disc and a few dark boats do work that a more detailed picture might distribute across dozens of objects. Elsewhere at the Marmottan, steam interrupts a station's ironwork and reflections complicate the edges of Monet's garden.

This selection follows the relation between firm structure and uncertain boundaries, but does not belong to Monet alone. Morisot lets garden light continue through a family group; Renoir organises a reader around a bright sheet of paper; an earlier studio scene assembles many students around one model. The twenty works offer several answers to what painting needs to describe clearly—and what it can leave less settled.
visitNote: Consult the museum's collection and exhibition pages before planning a visit. This selection includes paintings from several parts of the collection and is not a list of guaranteed displays.

books.title: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition
books.author: Anne Dayez, Michel Hoog and Charles S. Moffett
books.note: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition supplies historical context for Monet, Morisot, Renoir and Sisley. Use its entries to compare their subjects and methods rather than treating Impressionism as one uniform style.

works.title: Impression, Sunrise
works.catalogueTitle: Impression, sunrise
works.credit: Claude Monet. Impression, sunrise. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The orange sun stays distinct while much of Le Havre's harbour loses its edges in vapour. Dark boats and short reflections provide enough structure to locate the water. Shown in 1874, the painting's title supplied Louis Leroy with the word he used to mock the exhibitors. The historical label grew from this particular way of withholding detail.

works.title: Boats under Construction
works.catalogueTitle: Boats under Construction
works.credit: Berthe Morisot. Boats under Construction. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/berthe-morisot/boats-under-construction
works.description: The unfinished hulls reveal the structures that a completed boat normally covers. Rigging and supports add diagonals across the shoreline, giving the harbour a working rather than exclusively scenic character. Morisot makes construction visible through these exposed relations; the boats are recognisable even before they have acquired their finished surfaces.

works.title: Eugène Manet and His Daughter at Bougival
works.catalogueTitle: Eugene Manet with his daughter at Bougival
works.credit: Berthe Morisot. Eugene Manet with his daughter at Bougival. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/berthe-morisot/eugene-manet-with-his-daughter-at-bougival
works.description: Father and daughter share a small area around the garden table while bright foliage continues behind them. The closely spaced marks pass through clothes and vegetation, making the family group part of the same light as its surroundings. Their activity organises the portrait without requiring either person to turn outward in a formal presentation.

works.title: Shepherdess Resting
works.catalogueTitle: Shepherdess Resting
works.credit: Berthe Morisot. Shepherdess Resting. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/berthe-morisot/shepherdess-resting-1891
works.description: The long skirt carries the reclining body into the greens and browns of the ground. One arm supports the head, identifying rest through a simple physical arrangement. The figure remains distinguishable even where the surrounding marks are similar, so the relationship between body and grass can soften without becoming a loss of form.

works.title: Water-Lily Pond
works.catalogueTitle: Bassin aux nymphéas
works.credit: Claude Monet. Bassin aux nymphéas. Image credit: Claude Monet; https://www.marmottan.fr/notice/5105/?is=true. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:BASSIN_AUX_NYMPH%C3%89AS_(1918-1919)_Claude_Monet_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Marmottan_Monet_(W_1882).jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The division between bank and water is repeatedly disturbed by reflections and dense strokes of colour. Red, green and pale marks occupy the same active surface. The garden remains identifiable, but recognition is continually renewed rather than secured by one clear horizon or outline. The painting makes that difficulty part of sustained looking.

works.title: Boats in the Port of Honfleur
works.catalogueTitle: Bateaux dans le port de Honfleur
works.credit: Claude Monet. Bateaux dans le port de Honfleur. Image credit: Claude Monet; https://www.marmottan.fr/notice/5022/?is=true. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bateaux_dans_le_port_de_Honfleur,_Esquisse_(1917)_Monet_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Marmottan_Monet_-_W1846.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Masts and the church spire divide the low sky above the boats and waterfront houses. Their narrow verticals give detail to a view otherwise arranged in broad bands. The museum catalogue dates this work to 1917; that recorded date should not be silently replaced by an earlier year inferred from expectations about Monet's harbour painting.

works.title: Bouquet of Flowers
works.catalogueTitle: Bouquet de fleurs
works.credit: Paul Gauguin. Bouquet de fleurs. Image credit: Paul Gauguin; musée Marmottan-Monet [1]. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Paul_Gauguin_-_Bouquet_de_fleurs_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Marmottan-Monet.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The bouquet forms a compact upper mass, while the vase, cloth and fruit provide a less crowded base. Red and blue flowers give the arrangement weight through colour rather than individually isolated botanical detail. The balance between those two densities keeps the still life from becoming equally busy across its whole surface.

works.title: Claude Monet Reading
works.catalogueTitle: Claude Monet lisant
works.credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir. Claude Monet lisant. Image credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir; Source credit: Own work , user:Rlbberlin. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The paper catches light close to Monet's hands while his hat partly encloses the face. Renoir presents a painter absorbed in reading, with no need for a palette to identify a professional role. The portrait's activity turns inward toward the sheet, making the sitter's attention available without demanding his reciprocal gaze.

works.title: Interior of Gros's Studio
works.catalogueTitle: Intérieur de l'atelier de Gros
works.credit: Auguste Antoine Massé. Intérieur de l'atelier de Gros. Image credit: Auguste-Antoine Massé. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Many students look toward one seated model, their easels and raised hands occupying different parts of the high room. The model's separation explains the studio's collective organisation. What appears crowded is also purposeful: several acts of study depend on the same visible body, seen from positions that cannot all provide the same view.

works.title: The Arno Valley from the Paradisino at Vallombrosa
works.catalogueTitle: La vallée de l'Arno vue depuis le Paradisino de Vallombrosa
works.credit: Louis Gauffier. La vallée de l'Arno vue depuis le Paradisino de Vallombrosa. Image credit: Louis Gauffier. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The terrace wall separates the figures' immediate place from the broad valley beyond. That boundary gives the landscape a vantage point, making its extensive distance something viewed from somewhere particular. Gardens, woods and hills can then recede on a scale different from the small group standing near the foreground edge.

works.title: The Outer Boulevards, Snow Effect
works.catalogueTitle: Les boulevards extérieurs. Effet de neige.
works.credit: Camille Pissarro. Les boulevards extérieurs. Effet de neige.. Image credit: Camille Pissarro; musée Marmottan-Monet [1]. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Camille_Pissarro_-_Les_boulevards_ext%C3%A9rieurs,_effet_de_neige_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Marmottan-Monet.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Snow softens buildings and traffic without bringing the boulevard to a halt. People and carriages remain active among bare trees, their darker marks held within a restricted range of pale tones. Weather alters the city's visibility while leaving its use recognisable, a balance different from a landscape emptied of daily movement.

works.title: Berthe Morisot Reclining
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait de Berthe Morisot étendue
works.credit: Édouard Manet. Portrait de Berthe Morisot étendue. Image credit: Édouard Manet; Source credit: Unknown source Unknown source. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The pale face appears within a larger dark mass of clothes, hair and hat, set against red. That economy makes small changes around the eyes and mouth especially consequential. The portrait gains its presence through a few strong relations rather than through an extensive setting or a detailed account of the sitter's occupation.

works.title: Portrait of Julie Manet
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait de Julie Manet
works.credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir. Portrait de Julie Manet. Image credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir; musée Marmottan-Monet [1]. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Auguste_Renoir_-_Portrait_de_Julie_Manet_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Marmottan-Monet.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Long hair and a dark dress give the portrait a settled lower structure, while the slight turn of the face keeps it from becoming symmetrically frontal. The softly worked background supplies little competing information. The sitter's individuality is carried through this direction of attention, not through a symbolic object added beside her.

works.title: Mademoiselle Victorine de Bellio
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait de Mademoiselle Victorine de Bellio
works.credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir. Portrait de Mademoiselle Victorine de Bellio. Image credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir; Source credit: Gianluca T.. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The red blouse establishes the portrait's largest warm area. Above it, the face is built from smaller and softer changes, so it remains distinct without needing an equally sharp division at every edge. The pale background gives those differences room, keeping the clothing prominent without allowing it to replace the sitter.

works.title: Spring near Paris: Apple Trees in Blossom
works.catalogueTitle: Printemps aux environs de Paris. Pommiers en fleurs
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. Printemps aux environs de Paris. Pommiers en fleurs. Image credit: Alfred Sisley; musée Marmottan-Monet [1]. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Alfred_Sisley_-_Printemps_aux_environs_de_Paris,_pommiers_en_fleurs_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Marmottan-Monet.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The flowering trees repeat across grass and cultivated ground, providing a structure that the pale blossoms partly dissolve. Behind them, the darker hill keeps the light growth from merging with the whole distance. Spring becomes visible through a change in familiar tree forms, rather than through an added seasonal anecdote.

works.title: Volterra: Road Descending from the Town
works.catalogueTitle: Volterra. Route descendant de la ville
works.credit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot. Volterra. Route descendant de la ville. Image credit: Jean-Baptiste Camille Corot; musée Marmottan-Monet [1]. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jean_Baptiste_Camille_Corot_-_Volterra._Route_descendant_de_la_ville_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Marmottan-Monet.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The road's curve connects the figure and nearer trees to the more distant town. Simple tonal changes and overlapping ground are enough to establish depth along that route. The small person measures the setting without supplying a separate drama; movement through the place already gives the view a useful direction.

works.title: Indian Summer near Moret-sur-Loing
works.catalogueTitle: Été de la Saint-Martin, environs de Moret-sur-Loing
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. Été de la Saint-Martin, environs de Moret-sur-Loing. Image credit: Alfred Sisley; Source credit: Gianluca T.. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: Tall trees divide the landscape into narrow intervals beside the watercourse. Warm foliage catches attention against cooler areas farther away, making seasonal colour a means of separating distance. The repeated uprights remain important even where their leaves vary, holding together a view that could otherwise fragment into patches of warmth.

works.title: At the Ball
works.catalogueTitle: Au bal
works.credit: Berthe Morisot. Au bal. Image credit: Berthe Morisot; https://www.marmottan.fr/wp-content/themes/marmottan2019/collection/full/4020.jpg. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Au_bal,_par_Berthe_Morisot.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The open fan both belongs to the sitter and partly screens her. Its spread alters the portrait's outline, drawing attention toward the face while also interrupting access to it. Pale dress and skin remain distinct amid darker hair and plants. An ordinary accessory becomes an active part of how the person is presented.

works.title: The Pont de l'Europe, Gare Saint-Lazare
works.catalogueTitle: Le pont de l'Europe. Gare Saint-Lazare.
works.credit: Claude Monet. Le pont de l'Europe. Gare Saint-Lazare.. Image credit: Claude Monet; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Claude_Monet,_1877,_Pont_de_l%27Europe_(cropped).jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Iron structures give the station a firm framework, then steam makes parts of it difficult to see. The diagonal bridge remains legible above the changing white masses. Industry and atmosphere are inseparable subjects here: the machines produce some of the very air through which their architecture must be painted.

works.title: Arm of the Seine near Giverny, Sunrise
works.catalogueTitle: Bras de Seine près de Giverny, soleil levant
works.credit: Claude Monet. Bras de Seine près de Giverny, soleil levant. Image credit: Claude Monet; musée Marmottan-Monet [1]. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Claude_Monet_-_Bras_de_Seine_pr%C3%A8s_de_Giverny,_soleil_levant_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Marmottan-Monet.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The banks and their reflections approach one another in blue and violet, leaving a pale opening as the river's clearest indication. Water is understood partly through the space the trees do not occupy. The difficulty of locating a firm boundary gives the scene continuity without turning it into a uniformly undifferentiated surface.

closingSections.title: Start with a boundary
paragraphs: Choose one edge—a face against a hat, steam against iron or a tree against its reflection—and follow where it becomes clear or uncertain. That comparison works across several artists without implying identical methods. Check the museum's current display and loans before planning a visit around a particular painting.
